Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

rtists 0.1.0

  • Initial CRAN release.
  • Added plot3d(), an S7 generic with methods for fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, and fiber::bundle_set objects.
  • Two htmlwidget backends are available through backend (three.js is the default):
    • "threejs": a self-contained three.js renderer (no CDN). radius > 0 draws real world-space tubes with per-point colour and object-level depth-sorted transparency; the fast line mode scales to large bundles.
    • "plotly": a single scatter3d trace separated by NA break-points, retained as an interim fallback.
  • Colour modes supported by plot3d():
    • "orientation" (default): per-point RGB colour derived from the local fibre direction using the standard DTI convention (left–right = red, anterior–posterior = green, superior–inferior = blue).
    • Metadata key: any key from @point_data or @streamline_data can be mapped to a continuous (palette) or categorical colour scale.
    • Fixed colour: any CSS colour name or hex string.
  • Interactive figures support pan, rotate, and zoom.
  • The three.js backend now shows an on-scene toolbar (top-left, plotly-style) with controls to toggle the coordinate axes, download the view as a PNG, choose an orbit mode (rotate / pan / zoom), zoom in and out, re-frame the view to the data, and reset the camera. Disable it with plot3d(..., toolbar = FALSE).
  • The three.js legend panel includes a palette picker: a swatch icon per available palette, clickable to re-ramp the fibres live. It applies to continuous attributes, discrete (categorical) attributes, and per-bundle colouring alike, and it is seeded with the initial colour mapping from plot3d(). The curated set defaults to the CVD-safe perceptual palettes (Viridis, Plasma, Inferno, Cividis, Mako, Rocket, Mint), each flagged as such in the picker, alongside the diverging RdYlBu and Spectral.
  • Thin-line rendering is no longer scale-blind: when no radius is supplied (the fast line2 path), the default linewidth is auto-sized to approximately 0.5% of the scene’s bounding-box diagonal instead of a fixed 2 world units. A 2-unit slab was a hairline on a full-size DTI scene but covered most of the viewport on unit-scale synthetic scenarios, drawing giant overlapping quads and slowing rendering. Pass an explicit numeric linewidth to keep exact world-unit widths; the plotly backend uses a fixed width of 2 pixels when linewidth is left automatic.
  • Added plot2d(), an S7 generic with methods for fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, and fiber::bundle_set objects. It renders a static ggplot2 arclength projection: each streamline is re-parametrized by distance travelled along the fibre and the X/Y/Z coordinates are drawn against it in three vertically stacked facets, making it easy to compare tract geometry with per-point diffusion profiles (FA, MD). Geometries are downsampled into equal-arclength chunks (n_chunks), and the same colour vocabulary as plot3d() applies: orientation (DTI convention), any metadata key (continuous or categorical), or a fixed colour.

Bug fixes

  • The static (non-Shiny) htmlwidgets path is fixed: with the three.js backend, the ESM renderer module is imported asynchronously, which can register its widget binding after htmlwidgets’ initial staticRender() (run once on DOMContentLoaded). The console and Viewer pane therefore produced no canvas and no error. The loader now re-invokes Shiny’s binding scan or HTMLWidgets.staticRender() once the module is ready. The re-render is idempotent, so other widgets are left untouched.
  • Named bundles are honoured correctly in plot3d(): the per-bundle input names recorded by fiber::bundle_set() are now read from the right slot (@bundle_data), so a bundle_set built from a named list keeps its names instead of falling back to sequential indices.
  • The three.js legend no longer lists the bundle name twice: for bundle_set objects the dedicated per-bundle “Bundle” colour mode and visibility list already cover BundleName, so the name is excluded from the attribute “Color by” entries. A bundle_set with no other attributes still ships the per-bundle payload so the legend can show and toggle bundles.
  • The three.js legend rebuild no longer crashes when tooltip = FALSE is combined with a colour legend. The segment -> point map (segToPoint) is now shipped whenever a tooltip or a legend is present (previously only with a tooltip), so the legend’s live buildLine2Mapped() rebuild finds the map it needs. The renderer also derives the map from the per-streamline point counts when a payload omits it, so older serialized payloads degrade gracefully instead of throwing mid-render.
